newsitem.title: MALTA: Methode Electronics takes over Malta firm.
newsitem.headline: Methode Electronics takes over Malta firm.

text.p: Maltese automotive switch manufacturer Merit-Malta said on Wednesday it had been taken over by Chicago-based Methode Electronics Limited for an undisclosed amount.

Merit-Malta managing director Jost Merten said the decision to sell to the U.S. company, which also produces automotive switches, was taken after months of searching for a company Merit could itself take over, without success.

"We tried to buy many companies, including our ex-parent company (Merit-Werk of Germany), but they turned us down. There are not many good companies of our size left. They either went bankrupt or have been taken over," he said.
Methode's executive vice-president, Ted Kill, said his company also recognised the need for globalisation.
Kill said both companies produced automotive switchgear but in different areas of the vehicle.

"In the joining of these technologies and the sharing of our respective strengths we will be able to offer our customers a complete array of switchgear which will enhance our core strength while maintaining the highest quality standards," he said.
"Merit-Malta's strength in this area is Europe, with crossover into North America and the Far East. Methode's strength is in North America, with crossover into Europe and the Far East," he said.
Methode Electronics employs 3,250 personnel worldwide and had a turnover of $308 million last year.
It produces component devices for producers of automobiles, electronic data processing equipment, computer networks, instruments, voice and data communications equipment and consumer electronics.
It has three plants in the U.S. and one in Scotland which serve the automotive industry and 14 manufacturing plants around the world which serve the electronics industry.
Merit-Malta originally formed part of the German Merit- Werk but split from it and became fully independent 10 years ago. It produces over 50 million switches annually.
